title: Beef Stew
subtitle: Slow-braised beef with root vegetables in a rich gravy
excerpt: Braising steak cooked slowly with carrot, swede, and potato in a thick, dark gravy made from beef stock and red wine. One of the most satisfying things to come out of a home oven on a cold evening.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef stew is one of the most universally prepared dishes in British home cooking. The French equivalent, boeuf bourguignon, uses wine as the braising liquid and lardons for fat. The British version relies more on vegetables and beef stock. The key cut is braising steak (also sold as chuck, skirt, or shin): these tougher, well-exercised muscles have enough connective tissue to break down into gelatine during slow cooking, giving the stew its rich, glossy body. Never use expensive quick-cook cuts here: they dry out.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large casserole dish with a lid.

content.text: Brown the beef in batches in a very hot pan with no crowding: each piece needs contact with hot metal to develop colour. Crowding drops the pan temperature and the beef steams rather than browns. This step adds the most flavour. The stew is done when the beef is completely tender and pulls apart easily when pressed with a spoon.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Season the beef with salt and pepper. Dust with flour. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per batch, without moving. Set aside.

In the same pan, fry the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute. Add the red wine and scrape up any browned bits. Add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Return the beef. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and transfer to the oven. Cook for 1 hour 30 minutes. Add the carrot and swede. Cover and cook for a further 45 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the beef pulls apart easily. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.
